newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - Merrill ups China Light.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Merrill ups China Light.

text.p: Merrill Lynch has raised its intermediate rating on China Light & Power Co Ltd (CLP) to neutral from reduce due to CITIC Pacific Ltd's purchase of a 20 percent stake in the utility company.
"Having CITIC as a shareholder could result in long-term earnings enhancement," it said in a report dated January 30.

Merrill raised its net profit estimates to reflect the interest income on the cash inflow from the CITIC placement but lowered its five-year earnings per share (EPS) compound growth estimate to 5.4 percent from 6.5 percent due to EPS dilution.
It expects net profit of HK$7.25 billion in 1997, raised from a previous estimate of HK$6.21 billion, and EPS of HK$3.17 compared with a previous forecast of HK$3.12.
For 1998, it forecast net profit of HK$9.40 billion compared with a previous forecast of HK$7.83 billion, but reduced its EPS forecast to HK$3.78 from HK$3.93.
Merrill said it was not convinced that the earnings boost from the CITIC link would be sufficient to compete with market growth rates.

"Given the low base growth expected for the company's domestic earnings, we think a tremendous number of deals need to be signed if CLP is going to come close to competing with market earnings growth rates," it said.
Merrill also said that China Light was one of the most expensive utilities in the region, trading at around 11 times 1997 earnings and 12.6 times 1997 pure utility earnings.

"Although we think that CLP is expensive compared with other China power plays, we believe that this transaction gives strong support to current valuations and consequently we have raised our intermediate rating from reduce to neutral," it said.
Merrill also said that after the CITIC deal, which should bring a cash infusion of HK$16.3 billion, China Light would have a net cash balance of HK$14.3 billion at the end of the year.
"We suspect that the pressure might be on to make a sizeable acquisition," it said, adding that the acquisition of an existing power station in China would be preferable.
China Light shares were down HK$0.10 at HK$36.50 in late trade on Tuesday.
